repository.name: zephyrtrade
repository.title: ZephyrTrade Wind-Market Lab
repository.description: Study synthetic wind forecasts, asymmetric offer decisions & reproducible revenue backtests through transparent lessons.
repository.summary: ZephyrTrade links synthetic wind forecasts, offer optimization, backtests, and a local browser/Python research app. The companion begins with a generic gross-versus-net calculation before the source’s asymmetric settlement model.
repository.audience: Wind-energy students, forecasting researchers, and developers comparing hypothetical offer strategies.

model.equation: spread = b + 12 sin(2πt/12) + 5 sin(2πt/5); edge = spread − fees − slippage; P&L = notional · edge/10000.
assumptions: All prices, spreads, and returns are synthetic; no exchange or trading API is connected.
P&L is one hypothetical opportunity at the selected time, not accumulated realized performance.
Execution latency, inventory, liquidity, funding, and exchange risk are omitted.
Every spread, cost, and notional input is synthetic; no market data or trading connection is used.
The native source has separate forecast-error and market-value metrics; a higher toy P&L does not establish a better wind forecast.
The retained native observations have documented filtering and gaps. Neither this exercise nor a perfect-foresight benchmark establishes live trading performance.
model.introduction: The browser is a generic USD/basis-point sensitivity exercise. It does not execute ZephyrTrade’s DKK/MWh settlement, production scenarios, weighted-quantile offer, trained forecasts, or retained backtest snapshot.

modules.title: Separate forecast quality from economic value
modules.objective: Identify the units and objective behind a reported wind-market result.
steps: Read the native regression and revenue metric entry points in evaluate.py.
Apply 30 bps base spread, 10 bps fees, 5 bps slippage, and 10,000 USD notional.
At time zero, reconcile gross spread, total costs, net edge, and hypothetical P&L.
modules.reflection: Why can a forecasting model with a smaller RMSE still yield a different ranking under asymmetric imbalance prices?

modules.title: Stress an economic assumption
modules.objective: Explain why a gross opportunity is sensitive to the cost model.
steps: Retain the base spread and notional but raise slippage from 5 to 25 bps.
Predict the sign change in the opening opportunity before running.
Read validate_price_order and critical_fractile in the native optimizer; distinguish its asymmetric settlement prices from this toy slippage cost.

checkpoints.label: Opening net edge becomes negative 5 bps

modules.reflection: Which source variables determine the native optimal production quantile, and why is it not generally the mean forecast?

modules.title: Separate exposure size from strategy skill
modules.objective: Show that scaling exposure changes money at risk without improving per-unit economics.
steps: Keep the stressed 30/10/25 bps assumptions and increase notional to 40,000 USD.
Predict how costs and P&L scale while the net edge stays unchanged.
Read the native perfect-foresight description and identify why it is an upper-bound reference rather than an operational forecast.

checkpoints.label: The larger exposure loses 20 USD in the opening toy case

modules.reflection: What would a fair native strategy comparison need to hold constant across methods, timestamps, and price observations?

modules.title: Create a source-backed offer-study record
modules.objective: Document scenario assumptions and distinguish numerical parity from performance validation.
steps: Apply 50 bps base spread, 10 bps fees, 10 bps slippage, and 10,000 USD notional.
Run to twelve hours and export this single synthetic opportunity with its units.
Read the source data boundary and parity checker; prepare a native study record containing production scenarios, probabilities, price order, interval duration, and filtering limitations.
modules.reflection: Why can Python/browser numerical agreement support implementation consistency while leaving forecast calibration and market performance unproven?

source.scope: This browser lab is a standalone teaching approximation. Use the linked source for the project implementation.
